izxXGuVL21o.summary: In Ars Technica's War Stories, Naughty Dog co-founder Andy Gavin explains how the team squeezed Crash Bandicoot onto the original PlayStation. They overwrote Sony library code in RAM, built custom animation compression, and streamed assets around slow seek times.
izxXGuVL21o.why: It is one of the most frequently recommended videos on HN for old-school game development hacks under tight hardware constraints.

iYJKd0rkKss.summary: A condensed film of Dick Proenneke's footage of building a cabin and living alone in the Alaskan wilderness, using hand tools and local materials. It draws on the 8mm films he shot himself.
iYJKd0rkKss.why: HN recommends it often and warmly, as an inspiring and peaceful view of self-reliance and handcraft, in threads on cabins, solitude and woodworking.

iRkZcTg1JWU.summary: Moleman 2 is a feature-length documentary about the demoscene, tracing its rise from 1980s Commodore 64 culture to modern real-time art. It explains the algorithms and creative process behind demos and intros.
iRkZcTg1JWU.why: Recommended whenever the demoscene comes up as a well-made, accessible history and tour of the art form.

id1WShzzMCQ.summary: Alan Kay's Stanford Startup School lecture covers his career at Xerox PARC and how to think about inventing the future. He goes through what came out of PARC and why companies fail to capitalize on such ideas.
id1WShzzMCQ.why: It is HN's standard answer to questions on creativity, finding problems and PARC history, valued for Kay's thinking about thinking.

i6Fr65PFqfk.summary: Cal Henderson's DjangoCon 2008 keynote, "Why I Hate Django", is a funny critique of Django from a Flickr architect. It touches on scaling topics such as database replication.
i6Fr65PFqfk.why: Recommended as a brilliant, hilarious talk, though not the most educational.

iFDe5kUUyT0.summary: Episode 4 of Mike Maloney's Hidden Secrets of Money, explaining how currency is created through a chain of IOUs among the Treasury, banks and the Federal Reserve. It covers bonds, Fed checks, debt, taxes and fractional reserve lending, from a gold-and-silver advocate's viewpoint.
iFDe5kUUyT0.why: Recommended, often in Bitcoin and monetary threads, as a clear introduction to how the US money system works, though it comes with a strong goldbug slant.

iFTWM7HV2UI.summary: Technosociologist Zeynep Tufekci argues that the machine-learning systems used to serve ads also decide what political and social information people see. She explains how opaque algorithms can nudge, segment and manipulate users, and warns that the real danger is powerful people using AI to control populations.
iFTWM7HV2UI.why: HN commenters cite it whenever engagement-optimizing feeds, micro-targeting or ad infrastructure come up, as an accessible warning about algorithmic amplification.

iwcYp-XT7UI.summary: Lex Fridman's two-hour podcast with George Hotz, founder of Comma.ai, covering openpilot, autonomous driving and Hotz's views on AI and technology.
iwcYp-XT7UI.why: HN recommends it for Hotz's reasoning on cameras versus lidar and for an opinionated, original thinker's overview of comma and openpilot.

iHzzSao6ypE.summary: CGP Grey explains how traffic jams come from human driving behavior such as tailgating and reaction delays, and how leaving gaps and smoothing speed would reduce congestion. It also touches on self-driving cars.
iHzzSao6ypE.why: HN cites it as a concise, well-illustrated explanation of traffic flow, in threads on congestion, self-driving cars and driving habits.

iD9xk3SDSYc.summary: Eon is a demoscene production by The Black Lotus, released at Revision 2019 and designed for an Amiga with OCS chipset, 512 kB chip and 512 kB fast memory. This is the party version, which has some known glitches.
iD9xk3SDSYc.why: HN holds it up as a showcase of what a stock Amiga 500 can do and as one of the best demos ever in technique and storytelling.

iGFqfTCL2fs.summary: A short video from the trafficwaves.org site showing how traffic jams and standing waves form, including the fight between cheaters and blockers at an exit-lane backup. It also touches on how individual driving behavior affects the flow.
iGFqfTCL2fs.why: HN likes it as a fun, clear explainer of traffic waves and of the benefits of leaving gaps while driving.

iukBMY4apvI.summary: A short screencast tour of JSPM, SystemJS and ES6 features, building a small app with the then-new JavaScript module and package tooling. It shows how JSPM works as a package manager, bundler and loader.
iukBMY4apvI.why: Commenters credit it with opening their eyes to JSPM and using it to choose build systems.

iffTJ1vPCSo.summary: Ronald Minnich of Google explains how UEFI firmware is a large closed attack surface and describes Google's work replacing it with Linux-based boot firmware. It also touches on Intel ME and other security coprocessors.
iffTJ1vPCSo.why: Recommended as the go-to talk on firmware security risks, Intel ME, and why replacing UEFI with Linux speeds up and hardens boot.

iDulhoQ2pro.summary: Yannic Kilcher walks through the Attention Is All You Need paper, which introduced the Transformer, a sequence model based solely on attention without recurrence or convolutions. He reviews the architecture and the paper's translation results.
iDulhoQ2pro.why: HN recommends it as an accessible, clear walkthrough of the transformer paper for people with some AI background.

i70wkxmumAw.summary: Tom Scott tells how John Reber's plan to dam San Francisco Bay was disproved by the Army Corps of Engineers' giant hydraulic Bay Model in Sausalito. The model showed the plan would have been dangerously wrong.
i70wkxmumAw.why: HN recommends it as a short, fascinating story of a scale model preventing a terrible engineering decision.

ibqiet6Bg38.summary: Alexei Navalny phones an FSB chemical-weapons specialist, posing as a senior official, and gets him to describe the 2020 Novichok poisoning and its cover-up. The video is in Russian; HN commenters point to English subtitles.
ibqiet6Bg38.why: Praised as a remarkable piece of social engineering, spoofed caller ID plus pretexting, that produced direct evidence of the poisoning.

iG9CE55wbtY.summary: Sir Ken Robinson argues, with humor and stories such as that of choreographer Gillian Lynne, that education systems undermine creativity and should be changed. It is one of the most viewed TED talks.
iG9CE55wbtY.why: HN refers to it constantly in schooling debates, as a favorite talk or as the basis for arguments about creativity, though some commenters dispute its conclusions.

iGbC5j4pG9w.summary: A mini-documentary by a Canadian living in Japan explaining how an average family can afford a new detached house in Tokyo. It covers how houses are treated as depreciating assets and how Japanese zoning and building practices keep prices low.
iGbC5j4pG9w.why: It is the standard citation in HN housing debates for showing that dense cities can still have affordable single-family homes.

iJfw6lDlTuA.summary: Leonard Susskind opens Stanford Continuing Studies' Theoretical Minimum series with an introduction to quantum mechanics, a course for people who want real physics rather than popularization. It assumes some calculus and linear algebra.
iJfw6lDlTuA.why: HN recommends the series as an entertaining, serious route into physics for self-learners comfortable with basic math.

iSVHp6CAyQ8.summary: CNBC gets a tour of ASML's cleanrooms in the Netherlands to see how its roughly $200 million EUV lithography machines are built. It covers exploding molten tin, ultra-flat optics and why only one company can make these systems.
iSVHp6CAyQ8.why: Frequently recommended as a good, approachable overview of ASML and semiconductor equipment.

ig_qpNfXHIU.summary: CGP Grey, adapting The Dictator's Handbook, explains how rulers keep power and why succession causes trouble when they die. It is the sequel to his video on the rules for rulers.
ig_qpNfXHIU.why: HN recommends it as a 101-level crash course on the keys to power, and says it changed how some viewers see political discourse.

ipVxxxqwBQw.summary: Kurzgesagt examines who is responsible for climate change, comparing historical, current and per-capita emissions by country. It argues that individual footprints are a distraction from larger responsibility.
ipVxxxqwBQw.why: Recommended as a nuanced, data-backed treatment of emissions responsibility, made with Our World in Data.

iw17c70uJes.summary: A 60fps capture of Future Crew's 1993 MS-DOS demo Second Reality, one of the best-known pieces of the demoscene. It runs about 16 minutes of real-time graphics and music effects on PC hardware of the era.
iw17c70uJes.why: HN commenters cite it as the landmark demo of the demoscene's golden era, and this capture lets people watch it without running it under DOS.

i1vbvikDiI8.summary: The first part of a series on programming in Jai, Jonathan Blow's in-development language. It covers compiling, writing hello world and using code from other files.
i1vbvikDiI8.why: Jai had no public release, so commenters point to this beta user's videos as a way to see what the language is actually like.

iRleB034EC8.summary: Peter Robinson interviews Peter Thiel at the Hoover Institution about Thiel's essay The Straussian Moment. Thiel discusses how people trust the will more than the intellect and reason, and how the question of human nature has been abandoned.
iRleB034EC8.why: HN points to it as a primer on Thiel's thinking and as an example of Peter Robinson's skill as an interviewer.

iRsSjh5TTqI.summary: Tolgahan Cogulu demonstrates a fixed-fret microtonal guitar, playing music that uses notes between the usual twelve semitones. The channel is dedicated to his microtonal guitar designs.
iRsSjh5TTqI.why: Linked in music theory and tuning threads as a listenable example of microtonal guitar that sounds good.

ihkRwArnc1k.summary: First part of a four-part video history of Japan's electronics industry, covering the birth of the transistor and the rise of Japanese semiconductors. It appears to draw on NHK documentary material.
ihkRwArnc1k.why: Recommended in documentary and semiconductor-history threads as a detailed look at Japan's chip industry.

imhUmLtlZpw.summary: Economist Martin Jacques offers three building blocks for understanding China's rise, including seeing China as a civilization-state rather than a nation-state. He also covers how Chinese people view the state.
imhUmLtlZpw.why: HN recommends it in discussions of China's surveillance and social-credit systems for explaining Chinese attitudes toward the state.

ipzR9bhei_o.summary: Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor on organ, shown with a Music Animation Machine bar-graph score instead of traditional notation.
ipzR9bhei_o.why: Recommended as a music visualization that makes the structure easier to follow than sheet music.

i9i47sgi-V4.summary: Perun analyzes how corruption and theft in defence procurement hollowed out the Russian military before its invasion of Ukraine. It explains the mechanics of graft and how it degrades capability.
i9i47sgi-V4.why: Recommended as a long but insightful explanation of how corruption works inside institutions.

iIpPuJ_r8Xg.summary: Wendover Productions explains how the US military moves people and materiel worldwide, including prepositioned equipment, sealift and airlift. It shows the scale of the logistics system behind US force projection.
iIpPuJ_r8Xg.why: Recommended as a clear overview of military logistics, often as a contrast with civilian infrastructure efforts.

iLmkec_4Rfo.summary: A clip from the documentary Page One in which New York Times reporter David Carr interviews and confronts the founders of Vice magazine over their media deal. It captures tension between old and new media in 2010.
iLmkec_4Rfo.why: Brought up whenever Vice is discussed, as a memorable scene of Carr pressing its founders.

ieb1lmm9xHk.summary: A 1970 demonstration of W. Timothy Gallwey, author of The Inner Game of Tennis, teaching a complete beginner to play tennis in about ten minutes. He chats with her, feeds balls and gives positive feedback instead of instruction.
ieb1lmm9xHk.why: HN commenters use it as a vivid demonstration of learning by quieting the conscious mind, and recommend it alongside the book.

ip641WmY4pA.summary: A two-minute demo of SmartKnob View, an open-source input knob built from a brushless gimbal motor, magnetic encoder and round LCD. Closed-loop torque control gives software-defined detents and end stops.
ip641WmY4pA.why: HN people hold it up as a polished solo hardware project and the go-to example of haptic knobs, including in discussions of physical car controls.

iphcyNWFD10.summary: Veritasium explains in detail how LIGO detects gravitational waves, with a laser interferometer measuring displacements smaller than a proton. The video focuses on the extreme precision and the techniques needed rather than the general discovery story.
iphcyNWFD10.why: HN recommends it as a good layperson explanation of how LIGO's detection works and why it is so hard.

iqddnwKF8HQ.summary: JetBrains interviews Zig creator Andrew Kelley about why Zig has no 1.0 after a decade, why the project left GitHub, and why it bans AI contributions. He also covers what makes Zig better than C and his views on open source.
iqddnwKF8HQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a convincing primary-source interview showing Zig's cohesive design vision and the creator's level-headed reasoning.

i5uSbp0YDhc.summary: A long video essay on the claim that chemicals such as atrazine are feminizing frogs. It covers the science, the EPA and the role of chemical companies.
i5uSbp0YDhc.why: Cited as support for the claim that chemicals affect amphibian sex and as an example of corporate influence over regulation.

i9MHigUZKEM.summary: Dan Wahlin's hour-long beginner course on AngularJS builds a small single-page app while covering SPAs, directives, filters and data binding. It gives an initial grounding in Angular 1.
i9MHigUZKEM.why: HN recommended it as a good beginner screencast and as an example of the kind of tutorial other frameworks needed.

i9MXYZh1jcs.summary: debuglive makes a 1990-style dance track on an Amiga 500 with a Stereo Master sampler and cheap secondhand records, showing how sampling and trackers worked within tight memory limits.
i9MXYZh1jcs.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear demonstration of Amiga-era sampling and tracker workflows.

iN1MsCXkPSA.summary: Bob Nystrom shows his process for hand-drawing the diagrams in his book Crafting Interpreters, from pencil sketches to tracing and inking. It is a time-lapse of the whole illustration workflow.
iN1MsCXkPSA.why: Shared in Crafting Interpreters threads because it shows the care behind the book and is satisfying to watch.

iRdwXQb7CfM.summary: About Here explains how North American building codes requiring two staircases make small multi-story apartment buildings hard to build, and contrasts this with places that allow single-stair designs.
iRdwXQb7CfM.why: HN commenters share it in housing and single-stair egress threads as an enjoyable, accessible explainer of the two-stair rule.

iSmkqocn0oQ.summary: A short clip of Simon Peyton Jones talking about the future of programming languages, saying Haskell is useless in the sense that pure programs cannot have effects, while mainstream languages are useful but unsafe. He describes languages converging, with ideas such as STM and LINQ moving between them.
iSmkqocn0oQ.why: HN cites it constantly in language debates for his useful-versus-safe diagram and the convergence of languages, with commenters clarifying that his remark predates how Haskell handles effects.

i_qE1iAmjFg.summary: Paul Irish walks through the jQuery source code and shares ten lessons and interesting techniques from it, aimed at JavaScript developers who want to learn from a widely used library.
i_qE1iAmjFg.why: A classic recommendation among JavaScript talks and for reading real library code to learn patterns.

ia8Q51ouA_s.summary: A KRAZAM comedy sketch in which a character recites reassuring affirmations to site reliability engineers, satirizing on-call and outage culture.
ia8Q51ouA_s.why: Shared as comic relief that hits close to home for people who work with infrastructure at scale.

ir0FAa8P2MU.summary: The 1998 HBO dark comedy based on Col. James Burton's book about the 17-year development of the Bradley fighting vehicle. It satirizes how military procurement goes wrong.
ir0FAa8P2MU.why: It is recommended in threads on the F-35 and defense procurement as a funny, mostly factual look at how requirements balloon, with some warnings about its accuracy.

isBYV6QWDIo.summary: Asianometry explains why India, a chip design powerhouse, cannot fabricate chips, tracing the 1980s government attempt to build a national semiconductor champion and how it collapsed. It includes the sabotage at the SCL fab.
isBYV6QWDIo.why: HN uses it as the source on India's early fab attempts, in threads about India's semiconductor ambitions.

ispyUPqqL1c.summary: Patrick Boyle examines why birth rates are falling in nearly every country and argues the standard explanations do not hold up. He presents data suggesting fewer couples forming is a major driver.
ispyUPqqL1c.why: HN users cite it as a data-rich look at falling fertility that points to declining coupling rather than people choosing fewer kids.

iuumnjJWFO4.summary: The BBC TV version of the Babel Fish passage from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, with Ford and Arthur aboard a Vogon ship, narrated over the show's hand-drawn animated Guide entry.
iuumnjJWFO4.why: HN points to it for the memorable hand-animated computer graphics, which still hold up, and as the TV rendition of a famous passage.

i4pxw4tYeCU.summary: ElectroBOOM examines whether 5G and other electromagnetic waves can harm people, explaining the EM spectrum and the difference between ionizing and non-ionizing radiation. It includes experiments and measurements in his usual humorous style.
i4pxw4tYeCU.why: HN links it as an entertaining, in-depth rebuttal to 5G health fears from an electrical engineer.

i7kh8pNRWOo.summary: Jonathan Blow gives a talk on techniques for dealing with lack of motivation, malaise and depression, originally on Twitch. He discusses observing and understanding negative emotions and thoughts.
i7kh8pNRWOo.why: HN cites it as the best motivation advice some commenters have heard, and it is often shared in procrastination threads.

iDbyYGrswtg.summary: In an IT Crowd episode clip, Moss and Roy convince Jen that the internet is a small black box. She believes it and carries it around.
iDbyYGrswtg.why: It is used as a recurring joke whenever threads touch on the internet as a physical thing, and sometimes praised as a favorite sitcom.

iY57ErBkFFE.summary: The secret project cutscene for The Planetary Datalinks from Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri, featuring a quote about free information flow as the safeguard against tyranny.
iY57ErBkFFE.why: Quoted in privacy and surveillance debates, and praised as some of the best science fiction writing in games.

ipAnwilMncI.summary: Alexei Navalny's team investigation into a vast palace allegedly built for Putin, including the history of the bribes behind it. It is in Russian, with English subtitles available.
ipAnwilMncI.why: Recommended as a well-produced investigation and cited as evidence of oligarch wealth around Putin.

iph500cPK28.summary: ElectroBOOM's Mehdi Sadaghdar responds to Veritasium's lamp-and-long-wire puzzle, analysing it as an electrical engineer. He covers where the original framing misleads and the role of stray capacitance.
iph500cPK28.why: HN commenters recommend it as the more rigorous, polite and complete treatment of the Veritasium puzzle, though one dissents that the original misleads people.

i-fvwg9zy08.summary: Val Bennett's reggae cover of Dave Brubeck's Take Five, titled The Russians Are Coming. It was used as the theme tune of The Secret Life of Machines.
i-fvwg9zy08.why: HN mentions it to identify the Secret Life of Machines theme music.

i3D7XYQExt0.summary: Numberphile's Ben Sparks works through the physics of a car crash, showing how kinetic energy grows with the square of speed and why stopping distance climbs so quickly as velocity increases.
i3D7XYQExt0.why: Used as a short explainer when people need to illustrate why speed matters so much in braking and crash severity.

i9jIsxQNz0M.summary: A short social experiment video in which people mimic the New York subway practice of workers pointing at signs and signals. It makes the point cheerfully.
i9jIsxQNz0M.why: It is linked in threads on pointing-and-calling and error prevention as a light illustration of the practice.

iCI3B5eT9NA.summary: Adafruit's Ladyada interviews Paul Horowitz, co-author of The Art of Electronics. He discusses how the book came about and the third edition.
iCI3B5eT9NA.why: Pointed to as a companion to the Art of Electronics book, for people curious about the authors.

iJ4yL6kaV1A.summary: Applied Science shows how telecentric and hypercentric optics differ from normal lenses, producing no or negative perspective. The video builds a telecentric system from a Fresnel lens and demonstrates a lens that can see around objects.
iJ4yL6kaV1A.why: Commenters cite it as the clearest demonstration of hypercentric lenses and of looking around objects with optics.

iOWamCtnwTc.summary: Two Minute Papers covers a paper on speeding up fluid and smoke simulation with convolutional networks. It contrasts the approach with earlier regression forest methods.
iOWamCtnwTc.why: It is cited as an early example of neural networks learning physics, and recalled during later discussions of AI video generation.

iOucwX7Z1HU.summary: Marcus du Sautoy of the BBC demonstrates the wisdom of the crowd, showing that averaging many guesses of jelly beans in a jar lands near the true count.
iOucwX7Z1HU.why: Used as a quick, convincing demonstration of crowd estimation when discussing aggregated judgment.

iSSRaIU9_Vc.summary: Samy Kamkar demonstrates OpenSesame, a device that opens many fixed-code garage doors in seconds by exploiting a newly found attack, built around a Mattel toy. The video explains the attack and which brands are affected.
iSSRaIU9_Vc.why: HN people cite it as a memorable example of a clever low-cost hardware hack and as a reason to admire Kamkar's work.

iYpl0QVCr6U.summary: Maciej Ceglowski's Web Directions 2015 keynote on website bloat, arguing that pages have grown far heavier than their content justifies. This is a re-upload of the original talk.
iYpl0QVCr6U.why: Brought up as the classic critique of web bloat whenever slow or heavy sites are discussed.

iZn3kCsw5D8.summary: Jeff Bell's Blender Conference 2018 talk on how Netflix's animated film Next Gen was produced using Blender. It covers the studio's pipeline and tooling.
iZn3kCsw5D8.why: Cited as evidence that Blender can power feature animation and for its look at a real production process.

i_mLxyIXpSY.summary: Technology Connections spends 22 minutes on the humble can opener and what its design shows about products and why people don't know what to look for. It uses an everyday tool to draw broader lessons.
i_mLxyIXpSY.why: It gets mentioned as a thought-provoking video that changes how you look at everyday objects, though HN mentions are sparse.

i_yJTCDU4uE.summary: Tyler Cowen interviews Peter Thiel about technological stagnation, innovation, and lessons from Zero to One. The conversation ranges over business, startups and how Thiel thinks about progress.
i_yJTCDU4uE.why: HN people point to it as a strong interview and as the source of Thiel's stagnation thesis.

ia7IKW0yuG0.summary: Y Combinator partners Michael Seibel and Dalton Caldwell discuss how startups shifted from attracting outsiders to status- and money-seeking conformists. They give advice for nonconformist founders.
ia7IKW0yuG0.why: Linked in threads about YC culture and big tech burnout, as YC partners themselves acknowledging the trend.

ii1jcLg-eIQ.summary: Paul Graham's lecture in the 'How to Start a Startup' course, covering counterintuitive parts of startups and how to have ideas. It is the video form of his essay 'Before the Startup'.
ii1jcLg-eIQ.why: HN people point to it as the video version of the essay and cite it for advice on building things with interested people before calling it a startup.

ipRvjS7q1DI.summary: An excerpt of Richard Feynman's 1985 lecture Q&A about whether machines can think. He discusses the difficulty of defining what computers can never do and compares machine intelligence to machines that don't copy animals.
ipRvjS7q1DI.why: HN uses it as an early authoritative take in debates about AI, reasoning, and AGI.

iptAkpqjtMQ.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing follows a single front suspension bolt through its life, from sketch and drawing through machining, testing, assembly and racing.
iptAkpqjtMQ.why: HN commenters cite it as an illustration of the extreme effort Formula One teams put into safety, performance and reliability for a single part.

isgu-VrD0oM.summary: Mark Nelson of Radiant Energy Group explains how France, a leader in decarbonization through nuclear power, mismanaged its fleet, and what policy and outages threaten its future.
isgu-VrD0oM.why: Used as background in nuclear energy threads for its account of French policy and the economics of the fleet.

iv-5mZ_9CPY.summary: A guest video by Welch Labs on 3Blue1Brown explaining how text-to-image and video models work. It covers CLIP, shared embedding spaces, diffusion models (DDPM, DDIM), conditioning, guidance and negative prompts.
iv-5mZ_9CPY.why: HN uses it as a clear explainer for diffusion mechanics, such as negative prompts and faster sampling, and for joint text-image encoders.

izvdO-zdlKg.summary: Autoline's John McElroy and Caresoft president Terry Woychowski look at the BYD Seagull, an electric hatchback that sells in China for about $11,500. Woychowski points out the cost-saving design and manufacturing choices, and McElroy takes it for a short test drive.
izvdO-zdlKg.why: HN commenters cite it as a concrete teardown-style explanation of how BYD builds a cheap EV and why Western automakers are worried.

i5f8bqYYwps.summary: The full 2010 D8 conference interview of Steve Jobs by Walt Mossberg and Kara Swisher. He discusses Flash, privacy, multitouch, payments and what motivates him.
i5f8bqYYwps.why: Commenters cite timestamps from it as a primary source for Jobs' views on specific topics.

i8ju_10NkGY.summary: Music video for the LazyTown song "You Are A Pirate" from the children's show. It is a short, catchy kids' number.
i8ju_10NkGY.why: Mostly dropped in as a joke or tongue-in-cheek reference about piracy.

i8xwLWb0lLY.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on food waste covers how producers, sellers and consumers throw away huge amounts of food, including sell-by dates and donation myths.
i8xwLWb0lLY.why: HN commenters reference it as a source in threads on food waste, donation and landfill methane.

iARHCxAMAO0.summary: Footage of a protest at the University of Toronto against a talk by Warren Farrell on men's issues, including protesters blocking attendees from entering. It is part of a series of videos on similar campus protests.
iARHCxAMAO0.why: HN cites it as an example of protesters physically obstructing a talk, mostly in arguments about campus free speech.

iE39q-IKOzA.summary: A short AI-generated parody video that imagines Harry Potter as a Balenciaga fashion campaign, made with Midjourney, ChatGPT and Eleven Labs voices. It became a viral meme.
iE39q-IKOzA.why: HN cites it as the original of the Balenciaga AI meme family and as an early viral AI mashup moment.

iGGOjD_OtAM.summary: Adam Something argues in four minutes that gravity batteries like Energy Vault, which lift concrete blocks with cranes, are a poor energy storage idea. He draws on a longer Thunderf00t debunk.
iGGOjD_OtAM.why: HN cites it as the go-to debunk when gravity storage projects appear, usually by commenters who think the idea is a dud.

iGLzWdT7vGc.summary: The full unedited 2003 ZDF television interview with David Foster Wallace, running about an hour and a half. He talks about literature, boredom, silence, television and what stories do.
iGLzWdT7vGc.why: Used as a source for Wallace quotes on fiction, silence, self and technology rather than recommended outright.

iGOAQli7tGc.summary: Rasmus Lerdorf marks 25 years of PHP at phpday 2019 with a look at the highlights and lowlights of the language. He argues for upgrading PHP versions, covering performance, static analysis, zero-cost profiling and dead code elimination.
iGOAQli7tGc.why: HN uses it as the primary source for PHP's origins as a templating system for C and for the story behind its inconsistent function design.

iHfJRON3b-w.summary: Comedy YouTuber Max Fosh stunts his way to briefly becoming the world's richest man by selling a tiny share in a company at an inflated valuation. It is a lighthearted prank video about paper valuations.
iHfJRON3b-w.why: HN mostly cites it as a joke or as a prior example of inflating a company's valuation through a small share sale.

iIiAAhUeR6Y.summary: Malcolm Gladwell's TED talk on how Howard Moskowitz found that there is no single perfect spaghetti sauce. He draws a larger point about choice, preference and happiness.
iIiAAhUeR6Y.why: Cited to argue that people do not know what they want and that markets should be segmented.

iItLpwkQMUQ.summary: A German STRG_F investigation into why child sexual abuse material stays online on forums, following a father whose daughter's abuse images were widely shared. The reporters tried to get the content removed by contacting hosters.
iItLpwkQMUQ.why: HN cites it as evidence that journalists could remove most of a forum's content with simple hoster requests, in debates about CSAM and Tor.

iJunxkln578.summary: A Just Have a Think video on the proposed 16 billion pound Xlinks project to build solar, wind and battery capacity in southern Morocco. It would send around 3.6GW to the UK by subsea HVDC cable as near-baseload power.
iJunxkln578.why: Cited as a concrete example of a big renewable-plus-interconnector project in threads about nuclear costs, grid interconnects and submarine cables.

iK6SS8CXYZo.summary: A short news clip of Bill Gates being hit with a pie in the face in Belgium around 1999.
iK6SS8CXYZo.why: HN mentions it as evidence of how disliked Gates was in the 1990s, usually in passing or as a joke.

iKcWu0tsiZM.summary: Neel Kolhatkar's satirical short film parodies modern education and political correctness. It shows how obsession with inclusive speech makes plain communication difficult.
iKcWu0tsiZM.why: It is cited as a comedic parody of diversity and inclusion initiatives in threads on those topics.

iPkJH6BT7dM.summary: The bank run scene from It's a Wonderful Life, in which George Bailey explains to depositors why the bank cannot pay everyone back at once.
iPkJH6BT7dM.why: Used as a classic analogy for fractional reserve banking and bank runs.

iQdDRrcAOjA.summary: A short scene from the film Clerks in which two characters debate whether the independent contractors killed on the second Death Star were innocent victims. It is a comedic discussion of moral responsibility.
iQdDRrcAOjA.why: Invoked as a joke or analogy whenever contractors or employees work for a morally dubious or doomed organization.

iWeu2dxHRDg.summary: Mark Rober's holiday video features the near-final version of his glitter bomb package, built to deter thieves. It is part of his series of elaborate revenge traps against porch pirates and car thieves.

iYWzMvlj2RQ.summary: A one-minute clip of Linus Torvalds telling Nvidia "fuck you" over its lack of support for Linux and open source. It is taken from a Q&A session.

iaSUOFleNRU.summary: A short clip from the film Spies Like Us in which unprepared characters take a CIA agent test and Chevy Chase cheats his way through it.

ifKbwDf51bA.summary: A short Washington Post compilation showing Fox News hosts shifting from doubting the coronavirus to calling it a public health crisis.
